text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.

Its songbook marks the refrain for everyone, "Tutti", and the first line of each verse for one voice, "Solo quasi extempore sed meme ritmo": as if made up on the spot, but in the same rhythm. The second line is marked "Solo capriccioso".

source.en: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (Hampton, Va., 1927), pp. 60 and 61, read from the scan

The same book files it among its "Hymns on Biblical Themes", marked "Poco allegro ritmo marcato": fairly lively, with a firm, marked rhythm.

source.en: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), p. 60, read from the scan
